options: The difference between P and D
The degrees remaining to −180° at crossover
ESC delay in degrees of phase
questions.explain: How many degrees remain to −180° at the unity-gain frequency: 45–60° is a good tune, 0 means sustained oscillations.

questions.q: How does a 5 ms pure delay affect the phase at 50 Hz?

questions.explain: Too little D or too much delay: an underdamped pole excited by a downward step.

questions.q: Why must the inner loop be faster than the outer one?
questions.explain: Otherwise the outer loop sees the inner loop's dynamics. The rule is 3–10× in bandwidth.

questions.q: What is the only way to raise P without oscillations?
questions.explain: The delay sets the limit on the phase margin.

questions.q: Slow oscillations at 0.5–3 Hz are a sign of:
options: Aliasing from a low logging rate
Too much I or a fast outer loop
questions.explain: An integrator gives −90° at low frequencies.

questions.q: What does feedforward give the loop?
options: A fast response to setpoint changes without waiting for an error
questions.explain: FF derives the command from the setpoint itself; the controller only catches up with the residual error.
